newsitem.title: USA: Hecla sees its 1998 silver at 8 mln ounces.
newsitem.headline: Hecla sees its 1998 silver at 8 mln ounces.

text.p: Hecla Mining Co said it expects its annual silver production rate to be in the range of eight million ounces by 1998.

In a presentation to analysts in New York, chairman and chief executive Arthur Brown said much of the production would come from the newly opened Greens Creek mine in Alaska, in which Hecla holds a 29.7 percent interest. The company issued a statement after the presentation.
Hecla expects Greens Creek to add about 3 million ounces of silver production for Hecla's share in 1997, at a cash cost of less than $2.50 per ounce, Brown said.
Additional production would also come from a potential expansion of the Lucky Friday mine in north Idaho, where a new underground deposit is currently being explored, the company said.
The deposit is accessible from the underground workings of the Lucky Friday mine, and any new ore would be processed through the Lucky Friday mill, which currently has excess capacity, Hecla said.
Brown said secondary access development work and resource characterization of the deposit will begin in 1997, and full production is possible in early 1998.
Hecla expects its Rosebud Mine 50-50 joint venture with Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp in Nevada to go into production in the second quarter of 1997.
At full production, the mine will produce a total of approximately 100,000 ounces of gold annually during its currently estimated five-year life, at a cash cost of under $200 per ounce, Brown said.
